topic: Explainer: how the Coloprice Colocation Index is built (sources, unit, citations, history, CC BY)

facts: v1 aggregates published market data (CBRE, JLL, operator disclosures); quarterly updates; each data point links to its source
Wholesale = committed IT load, USD per kW per month, excluding metered power
October 2026 release: 23 markets, median $200 per kW per month

Source per market: CBRE Global Data Center Trends 2026 — Singapore, Chicago, Frankfurt, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Sydney, Querétaro, Santiago, Bogotá, São Paulo, London, Amsterdam, Paris; CBRE North America Data Center Trends H1 2026 — Northern Virginia, Dallas–Fort Worth, Houston, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Atlanta, Silicon Valley, Hillsboro, New York Tri-State; CBRE North America Data Center Trends H2 2025 — North America (avg)
Tracking since 2023-06 · 302 data points (colocation and GPU price series)
Every refresh of the price data appends a point; if a value has not moved, no duplicate point is written until a week has passed; past points are never rewritten
Series that start before August 2026 are seeded from published third-party indices
Every figure on Coloprice is reproducible; if a number is not published by a primary source, it is left empty — nothing is estimated silently
Compiled data is free under CC BY 4.0 — cite Coloprice with a link

figure.label: one unit: USD per kW of committed IT load per month

slides.label: Step 1 · Collect
slides.text: Every price starts in a **published source**: CBRE and JLL market research and operator disclosures.

slides.label: Step 2 · Normalise
slides.unit: USD per kW of committed IT load per month
slides.context: Metered electricity is excluded, so markets compare like for like. Retail racks (3–5 kW) are tracked separately, as a monthly range.

slides.title: Step 3 · Cite every market
slides.unit: Markets per source report · October release
slides.footnote: 23 markets in total. Missing data stays empty: nothing is estimated silently.

slides.label: Step 4 · Keep the history
slides.unit: data points in the price history since June 2023
slides.context: Each refresh appends a point. Unchanged values are not repeated within a week, and past points are never rewritten.

slides.label: Step 5 · Publish it openly
slides.text: The compiled data is **free under CC BY 4.0**. Cite Coloprice with a link.
slides.attribution: Monthly releases and raw JSON series are public, so anyone can check the numbers.

slides.text: Every figure on Coloprice is reproducible and sourced.

caption:
23 markets, one unit: how the Coloprice Colocation Index turns market research into a comparable price per kW.

Every value starts in a published source, mostly CBRE and JLL research and operator disclosures. It is normalised to USD per kW of committed IT load per month, with metered power excluded, and each market links to its report. Missing data stays empty.

The price history holds 302 data points since June 2023, and past points are never rewritten. The data is free under CC BY 4.0.

Data: Coloprice index, history and methodology pages, Oct 2026. Sources on the last slide.
